enonce.texte:
Match the English emotion words with their French translations. Write the correct letter next to each word.

  • 1. Happy
  • 2. Sad
  • 3. Angry
  • 4. Tired
  • 5. Worried

French translations: A. fâché B. fatigué C. heureux D. inquiet E. triste

questions.texte: Match each English word with its correct French translation.

enonce.texte: Read each situation and identify the most appropriate emotion or feeling.

questions.texte: Your best friend is moving to another country. You will not see him/her for a long time. How do you feel?
Someone broke your favourite phone. You feel like shouting. What is your emotion?
You have an important exam tomorrow and you haven't studied enough. What do you feel?
You just received a gift that you really wanted. You are smiling. What is your emotion?
You walked a long distance under the hot sun. You want to sit down and close your eyes. What is your feeling?

enonce.texte: Complete the sentences with the correct adjective (feeling) or adverb (how you do something).

questions.texte: She cried _______ (sad) because her cat ran away.
He shouted _______ (angry) at his brother.
I felt very _______ (happy) when I saw my mother.
They looked at the sick child _______ (worried).
He yawned and spoke _______ (tired) during the meeting.

enonce.texte: Your friend tells you about a problem. Show empathy by responding appropriately.

questions.texte: Your friend says: 'I lost my wallet with all my money.' How do you respond?
questions.reponse: I'm so sorry to hear that! / That's terrible! / How can I help?

questions.texte: Your friend says: 'I got a promotion at work!' What is your empathetic response?
questions.reponse: That's wonderful! I'm really happy for you. / Congratulations!

questions.texte: Your friend says: 'I failed my driving test.' What do you say?
questions.reponse: Oh no! I'm sorry. Don't worry, you'll do better next time.

questions.texte: Your friend says: 'I have a headache and I feel sick.' How do you react?
questions.reponse: That's too bad. Take some rest and drink water.

intitule: Talking About What Makes You Feel Emotions

enonce.texte: Write a short paragraph (5-6 sentences) answering the questions below.

questions.texte: What makes you feel happy?
questions.reponse: I feel happy when I spend time with my family and friends. Also, when I eat good food or listen to music, I feel very happy.

sousQuestions.reponse: I feel sad when I see someone suffering or when I miss my family.
I feel angry when people are unfair or when they lie to me.
I feel worried when I have important exams or when a family member is sick.

enonce.texte: Read the following dialogues. Fill in the missing response with an appropriate expression of empathy or reaction.

questions.texte:
Person A: 'I'm really tired today. I worked all night.'
Person B: '___________________'
questions.reponse: Oh, you must be exhausted. You should take a rest.

questions.texte:
Person A: 'My grandmother is very sick.'
Person B: '___________________'
questions.reponse: I'm so sorry to hear that. I hope she gets better soon.

questions.texte:
Person A: 'I got 100% on my math test!'
Person B: '___________________'
questions.reponse: That's amazing! Congratulations! I'm really proud of you.

questions.texte:
Person A: 'I'm worried about my job interview tomorrow.'
Person B: '___________________'
questions.reponse: Don't worry. I'm sure you'll do great. Just relax and be yourself.

intitule: Creative Writing: A Letter of Emotion

enonce.texte: Write a short letter (150-200 words) to a friend describing a recent experience that made you feel one of the following emotions: happy, sad, angry, tired, or worried. Use at least 5 emotion adjectives and 3 adverbs in your letter.

questions.texte: Write a letter to a friend explaining an experience and how it made you feel.
questions.reponse: Dear [Friend's name], I hope you are doing well. Last week, I felt extremely happy because I passed my English exam with a very good grade. I was so excited and proud of myself! However, I also felt a little worried before the results came out. I studied hard and worked carefully, but I still had some doubts. When I finally saw my score, I smiled happily and called my mother immediately. She was also very happy for me. I also felt a bit tired after all the stress, but now I feel relieved. I am looking forward to celebrating with you soon! Take care, [Your name].
